name: King's Indian Defense
blurb: Black lets White build a big pawn centre, then attacks it with ...e5 or ...c5 and often storms the kingside. A dynamic choice against 1.d4.

ideas.d4 Nf6: Stops e4 for now and keeps Black's setup flexible.
ideas.d4 Nf6 c4 g6: Prepares ...Bg7. Black lets White build a big centre and plans to attack it later.
ideas.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7: The bishop goes to the long diagonal. The f6 knight blocks it for now, but it will bear down on the centre later.
ideas.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6: Stops e5, which would kick the f6 knight.
ideas.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O: Black castles early, so the king is safe before the centre opens.
ideas.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e: The key King's Indian break. The e5 pawn attacks d4 and fights for the centre.
Adds pressure on d4 and asks White to decide what to do with the centre.
The knight steps back to e7, where it supports ...f5 and can go to g6 later.
Clears the way for the f-pawn. With the knight gone from f6, Black can play ...f5.
Black hits e4 and starts the kingside pawn storm that is the main plan in this structure.
ideas.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3 O-O Be3 e5: Against the Sämisch, Black uses the same ...e5 break to hit d4.
ideas.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f4 O-O Nf3 c5: Against the Four Pawns Attack, Black hits White's big centre from the side before it rolls forward.
